title: NAR Metropolitan Median Area Prices and Affordability (Third Quarter 2026) — a lagging price restatement at 10:00 a.m. ET, on FOMC+1, behind Q3 GDP advance and PCE
source: IR: the publisher's own 2026 forward calendar — nar.realtor/press-releases/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule (HTTP 200, fetched direct 2026-09-08) and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11, text extracted this session), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "Thu., Oct. 29 | Third Quarter Metro Home Prices" under the standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time". Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-08 by the pending-home-sales-2026-09-17 sweep, on the precedent pending-home-sales-2026-09-17, pending-home-sales-2026-12-17 and existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 already set (NAR produces this series rather than reporting someone else's, so its forward calendar is primary). PROMOTED ON THIS SERIES' OWN EXECUTION RECORD, NOT ONLY ON THE SCHEDULE, and it is a stronger record than the one the PHSI lanes promoted on: all three 2026 quarterly editions that have already passed score EXACT to the day and the hour against their scheduled rows, read from NAR's own newsroom <time> elements — Q4-2025 data scheduled "Wed., Feb. 4" published 2026-02-04T09:00:00-06:00, Q1-2026 data scheduled "Tue., May 5" published 2026-05-05T09:00:00-05:00, Q2-2026 data scheduled "Tue., Aug. 4" published 2026-08-04T09:00:00-05:00. All three are 10:00 ET, and the UTC offset TRACKS DST (-06:00 in February, -05:00 in May and August), which independently shows the stamp is a real local-time publication time rather than a constant the CMS writes. 3 for 3 on this series versus 2 for 2 on PHSI, and it is an INDEPENDENT evidence stream from the PHSI record rather than more of the same. No conflicting NAR surface was found for this series. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The only 2026 edition of NAR's quarterly metro price series this calendar tracks; the other three (02-04, 05-05, 08-04) have passed. FOUR FINDINGS FROM INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08, D-51), and the useful ones are all about ATTRIBUTION rather than about the number. (1) THE NATIONAL HEADLINE IS NOT NEWS BY THE TIME IT PRINTS. NAR publishes the national median existing SINGLE-FAMILY price in every monthly Existing-Home Sales release (June 2026: $446,400, +1.8% y/y, published 2026-07-09T09:00:00-05:00), so by the September-data EHS on 2026-10-13 — sixteen days before this print — all three months of Q3 are already public from the SAME publisher. FHFA HPI lands 10-27 and S&P Cotality Case-Shiller 10-27 on the same quarter. Corroboration that the national reading is already agreed: Case-Shiller's national index posted +1.5% for June 2026 and NAR's own Q2 metro national median was +1.5% y/y ($434,900). What is genuinely new on 10-29 is the ~230-MSA cross-section and the affordability tables, neither of which any instrument here reads. (2) THE SESSION BELONGS TO OTHER EVENTS, MEASURABLY. 2026-10-29 is FOMC+1 (decision 10-28) and carries the Q3 GDP advance and PCE at 08:30, the ECB decision, and a 7y note auction — all before a 10:00 quarterly restatement. (3) THE GENERAL FOMC+1 WIDENING IS REAL BUT DOES NOT SHOW ON THE AUTUMN SUBSET. Re-measured this session from Yahoo daily bars 2014+ and the Fed's own FOMC calendars (115 decision dates scraped): on 96 FOMC+1 sessions ITB's median session range is 2.093% vs an 1.826% baseline (p=0.002; ex-2020 n=87, p=0.002), XHB 1.967% vs 1.609% (p=0.001), SPY 1.193% vs 0.864% (p<0.001), while |open->close| is null everywhere (ITB p=0.481, XHB p=0.212, SPY p=0.115) — wide, not directional, reproducing the pending-home-sales-2026-09-17 lane's independent measurement. BUT the October/November-meeting subset, which is the exact seasonal shape 10-29 sits in, is NULL on all three: ITB 2.039% (n=10, p=0.766), XHB 1.846% (p=0.697), SPY 0.871% (p=0.832). Registered as FT-nar-metro-home-prices-2026-10-29-2. (4) A CONFOUND KILLED BEFORE IT COULD BE INHERITED. This series' own three 2026 release days ran wide on ITB (median 2.665% vs 1.830%, p=0.108) — but all three sat in the first week of a month, and first-week sessions are systematically wide independent of any NAR release (ITB day<=5 median 1.916% vs 1.828% mid-month, n=508, p=0.039; XHB p=0.015; SPY p=0.002). Month-END sessions, where 10-29 sits, are null (ITB day>=26 1.785%, n=570, p=0.189; XHB p=0.712; SPY p=0.958). So the release-day widening is calendar placement, not the release, and it does not transfer here. (5) THE BUILDER COLLISION THAT THE SEPTEMBER PHSI LANE REFUTED DOES FIRE ON THIS DATE. Re-run EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates (caches busted 2026-09-08): DHI — ITB's largest holding — filed its FY Q4 on 2024-10-29 and 2025-10-28, a ~+28/29d lag off its 09-30 fiscal year end, pointing at 2026-10-28/29; PHM has filed Q3 in the 10-21...10-26 window in each of the last eight years (2025-10-21, 2024-10-22); NVR likewise (2025-10-22, 2024-10-22). Registered as FT-nar-metro-home-prices-2026-10-29-3.
